Free Programs Available Through Consumers Energy
Lenawee County residents have access to two great energy-saving programs through Consumers Energy. Both programs support homeowners and renters and include assistance to mobile homes. Read More about
Project Connect - Linking Lenawee with Vital Resources
Lenawee Continuum of Care will host Project Connect on Wednesday, October 28, from 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at the Merchant Building at the Lenawee County Fair & Event Grounds. Read More about
Blood Drive Coming to the Human Services Building
The American Red Cross will hold a blood drive on Monday, November 16, 2026, at the Lenawee County Human Services Building in Adrian. If you’re able to give, consider rolling up your sleeve and helping provide lifesaving blood for patients in need. Read More about
MDHHS Launches App to Help Residents Quit Tobacco
Michigan adults now have a new tool to help them quit tobacco. The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) has launched the QuitLogix app, bringing support straight to their phones. Read More about
Mental Health First Aid Training Offered in Lenawee County
Much like CPR prepares individuals to respond to a physical emergency, Mental Health First Aid helps people recognize and respond to mental health concerns. Read More about
Trick-or-Treat with Lenawee County at Our Trunk or Treat!
Lenawee County invites families from across the community to join us for a Trunk or Treat on Thursday, October 29, from 5:00 to 6:00 PM in the north parking lot of the Lenawee County Judicial Building. Read More about
Drive-Thru Drug Take-Back Day – Fall 2026
Safely dispose of your unused, unwanted, or expired medications this fall at the Drive-Thru Drug Take-Back Day hosted at Promedica Hickman Hospital. Read More about

Carbon Monoxide: Before You Turn on the Heat
Before you settle in for another Michigan heating season, take a few simple steps to help protect yourself and your family.
When Should You Keep Your Child Home from School?
During the fall, when colds, flu and other illnesses begin making their way through classrooms, it can be difficult to know when a child needs a day at home and when they’re well enough to head to school.
From Tailgates to Potlucks: Keep Fall Foods Safe
Whether you’re serving burgers from the back of a pickup truck, bringing your famous cheesy potatoes to a family gathering or setting out snacks for a Halloween party, a few simple food safety habits can make sure the only thing your guests take home is leftovers.
Septic System 101: What Every Homeowner Should Know
A properly maintained septic system quietly treats wastewater from your toilets, sinks, showers, washing machine and other household plumbing. But when something goes wrong, it can quickly become messy, expensive and potentially harmful to your family, your property and the environment.
Why Routine Checkups Matter (Even When You Feel Healthy)
Routine checkups aren't just for when something feels wrong. They're one of the best ways to stay healthy in the first place. Think of it like changing the oil in your car. You don't wait until smoke starts pouring out from under the hood before deciding it's time for maintenance. Your body deserves that same kind of attention.
Building Healthy School Lunches: Simple Choices That Help Kids Learn and Grow
Small, balanced choices can give children the energy they need to stay focused, learn, and play throughout the school day. A nutritious lunch provides more than just calories. It fuels growing bodies, supports brain development, helps maintain steady energy levels, and can even improve concentration and mood in the classroom.
Prepared, Not Panicked: Emergency Preparedness for Families
Summer in Michigan has a personality all its own. One minute it’s sunshine and backyard burgers. The next? The sky turns greenish-gray, the wind starts doing gymnastics with your patio furniture, and suddenly everyone is asking, “Did anyone charge the flashlight?”
Picnic-Perfect (and Safe): Your Guide to Outdoor Food Safety
Let’s keep your outdoor feast firmly in the “fond memories” category—not the “why does my stomach hate me?” category.
Flooded Basement, Hidden Risks: Health Hazards After Heavy Rain
From mold creeping into corners to unseen contamination on everyday surfaces, what lingers after the water recedes matters just as much as the flooding itself.
What Public Health Does for You Every Day
While you’re going about your routine, grabbing coffee, heading to work, making dinner, the Lenawee County Health Department is right there in the background, helping keep things safe, steady, and just a little bit healthier for everyone.
Know Your Numbers: Why Blood Pressure, Cholesterol, and Glucose Matter
Blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose may not sound exciting, but they’re basically your body’s behind-the-scenes report card. They tell you what’s going on inside, even when everything feels normal and life is humming along just fine. And yes, it’s completely possible for things to be a little off even when you feel great.
Nutrition on a Budget: Healthy Eating During the Post-Holiday Stretch
January often arrives with a mix of fresh intentions and tighter finances. After holiday meals, travel, and gift-giving, many households are looking for ways to stretch their grocery dollars while still eating well. The good news is that healthy eating does not have to be expensive. With a little planning and a few smart strategies, nutritious meals can fit into nearly any budget.
Germ Hotspots in Your Home You Might Be Missing
We all know germs are sneaky, but did you know some of the biggest culprits are sitting right in your own home? Let’s take a peek at some of the most common germ hangouts and how to send them packing.
Sniffles, Sneezes, or Something More? Sorting Out Cold, Flu, and Allergy Season
Ah, fall in Michigan—when the air gets crisp, the leaves crunch underfoot, and the tissue boxes start flying off the shelves. It seems like everyone you know is sniffling, sneezing, or coughing. But the real mystery is this: Do you have a cold, the flu, or are your allergies just staging a dramatic comeback?
Safe Handling, Safe Home: Reducing Firearm Risk
Whether you hunt, enjoy sport shooting, or keep a firearm for personal protection, the right to own and carry a gun comes with an important responsibility: keeping yourself, your loved ones, and your community safe.
The Link Between Environmental Health & Public Health
Our environment plays a crucial role in shaping public health. The air we breathe, the water we drink, the food we eat, and the spaces we live in all impact our well-being.
Protecting Our Children: Lead Poisoning Prevention and Treatment
Here’s what you need to know about preventing lead poisoning and how we’re here to help.
Why You Should Wash Your Hands Often (It's Not Just for Pandemics!)
It's an essential practice for maintaining overall health and preventing a variety of illnesses. Let’s dive into the reasons why this mundane practice deserves our ongoing attention.
The Crucial Role of Public Health and the Lenawee County Health Department
The first week of April is National Public Health Week and is a great time to review why we even have organizations focused on public health and why the Lenawee County Health Department began.
Get Tested, Stay Healthy
Unfortunately, many STIs can go undetected due to a lack of symptoms, leading to potential long-term health complications and increased risk of transmission to others.
